\begin{example} \end{example}[A 3-dimensional torus] ↗ thm:cellular-singular-homology-isomorphic 1. ch2:2.39\group Cellular Homology

For $T^3$, all cellular boundary maps vanish, so $H_i(T^3)$ is $\mathbb {Z}$ for $i=0,3$, $\mathbb {Z}^3$ for $i=1,2$, and zero otherwise. For $K\times S^1$, $d_3(c^3)=2C$, $d_2(A)=2b$, and $d_2(B)=d_2(C)=0$, giving $H_3=0$, $H_2\cong \mathbb {Z}\oplus \mathbb {Z}_2$, and $H_1\cong \mathbb {Z}^2\oplus \mathbb {Z}_2$. \end{example}
